page.layout: One column of running text in the centre. Small marginal notes stand in the left margin, beside the lines they belong to. The right margin holds only dark marks that look like show-through from the facing page, which are not transcribed. No heading, footnote or signature.

main_text.p: cedebant. Quòd si mari res agenda erat, tota hæc res ad extruendas & adornandas, armandasque triremes referebatur: & usu interdum vênit, ut singuli trecenorum ditissimorum poscerentur singulas triremes ædificare & instruere: id quod Demosthenes impensè suasit in oratione περὶ συμμοριῶν [?], quæ tota hoc de negocio loquitur, & quod suasit, etiam persuasit. Pertinentque ad eandem hanc rem duæ ejus orationes aliæ, contra Phænippum de permutatione, & de coronâ præfecturæ navalis. Et erant constituta præmia honoris iis, qui celerius ac promptius cæteris munus sibi commissum expedirent, ut difcimus cum aliunde, tum ex oratione jam dictâ de coronâ τριηραρχίας [?], id est, præfecturæ navalis, & ex oratione altera περὶ ἀντιδόσεως [?]. Nam τριηραρχία [?] significabat λειτουργίαν [?] illam inter reliquias difficillimam extruendæ & adornandæ triremis sumptu privato, & τριηραρχεῖν [?], munus illud pro republicâ obire, & τριηράρχημα [?] id, quod triremem instruendam impenditur: quemadmodum ἐπιτριηράρχημα [?], finitâ jam τριηραρχίας [?] supra τριη-

page.notes: The printed Greek is partly faint and was not read letter by letter. Every Greek word marked [?] is a best reading and must be checked against the scan. Greek words in the middle of the lines (for example the words after "ad" and "impensè") were not fully legible, so these readings are uncertain. The left margin holds small fragments of marginal notes (Greek and numerals, around lines 8 to 17 from the top). They are too faint and blurred to read reliably, so they are not transcribed. Some of these marks may be show-through from the other side of the leaf. The right margin holds dark vertical marks, probably show-through or the binding shadow, and they are not transcribed. The final word "τριη-" is broken at the line end and continues on the next page. The printed hyphen is kept. "difcimus" is transcribed as printed (long s as s). Possible printing error: "disceimus" is the probable intended reading, but the printed form is kept. The small mark "exa" at the bottom left, under the last line, is not clearly part of the text and was not transcribed. It may be a fragment of a note or show-through.
